an10.60:3.2: Read _sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccasaññā_, “perception of impermanence of all conditions” with BJT and PTS, also adopted by Bodhi. Editions vary; MS reads _anicchāsaññā_ (“perception of wishlessness”). However, the contemplation of “impermanence” regarding all conditions is well attested elsewhere (eg. [mn50:18.5](), [sn55.3:3.7](), [an4.163:2.2](), [iti85:2.3](), [mil6.4.1:7.4](), while _anicchā_ never appears in a similar context. The commentary’s silence here suggests that it read a common phrase not needing comment. Moreover, the Tibetan parallel (D 38 ka 276a6) also reads “impermanence” (_mi rtag pa’i ’du shes_; see Analayo, *Mindfully Facing Disease and Death*, p. 104, note 15).
an10.60:7.3: Not a question! I have corrected MS punctuation.
an10.60:7.4: BB evidently follows PTS dict in identifying daddu with ringworm, but the Skt dictionaries more commonly have either leprosy or herpes. http://sanskritdictionary.com/?iencoding=iast&q=dadru&lang=sans&action=Search I’m not sure how BB gets “cancer” for pilaka, but the Pali and Skt dicts have “boil, pustule, pimple”.
an10.60:11.2: reading viharati and upayupadana. The sequence of terms for defilements beginning with upaya express a gradual process.
an10.60:12.2: Compare [an3.39:3.2](), where an unenlightened person is similarly horrified when seeing the ravages of old age, not reflecting that they too are subject to the same. The Tibetan parallel has a similar reflection here.
